title: Keep Going: long-horizon terminal lab
mechanism: Explore, build, verify, then keep revising when a proxy score tricks you. TerminalHorizon long-horizon agents

title: Watch Then Plan: look, then pick the next step
mechanism: Closed-loop cooking board: look at the pan, then pick the next atomic step; open-loop plans drift

title: Sorry Free: be the prover, Lean is the judge
mechanism: Place tactics into glowing sorry rings and Lean snaps them shut or bounces them; dodge the restate-the-goal helper lemma, then bet Basic loop vs Full agent on an Erdős-hard toy goal under a $300 budget

title: Sharded Swarm: self-replicating AI on 4GB TV boxes
mechanism: Spatial AI lab: seat shards by RAM, route around weak links, enlist a 26B swarm under a clock where flaky uptimes drop on commit; unlock a daily pack→route→scale mix with a shareable score

title: Off the Trend: does Meta's Muse Wonder generalize?
mechanism: AI lab game: predict held-out scores, then hold knobs to think, tune or scale a base model and watch its point move against Spark 1.3's trend live; then weight the four real benchmarks into your own yardstick and flip the leader between Wonder Full and Opus 5.5

title: Physics Director: make AI video obey physics
mechanism: A physics simulator steers a frozen video generator: anchor the object early, guide the water softly

title: Be the LLM: why AI makes stuff up
mechanism: Behind the Scenes, 4 levels: guess a model's next word, reshape the odds with temperature (real softmax), cut the tail with top-p (real nucleus sampling), then watch it confidently invent a birthday. Toy probabilities, real math, sourced numbers (Holtzman et al. 2019; Kalai et al. 2025).

title: Fly Blind: look only when you must
mechanism: A 3-level drone game: fly on the drone's own drifting map, find hidden gaps, and spend as few depth looks as you can. Then watch an AI pilot do it. Toy game, real ALONE numbers (98%/97% success, depth on 0.9%/1.3% of steps).

title: Code holds the wall. Pixels forget it.
mechanism: A 3-level game: hide from an AI seeker in a code world (the engine owns your walls) and a pixel world (each frame is the state, so walls drift). Watch the AI write itself notes and bring a ramp, then outsmart it. Toy game, real AgentGarten numbers.

title: One letter the exome can't see
mechanism: A 3-level game: edit one DNA letter deep in an intron to wake a sleeping splice site, learn why a near-perfect site alone does nothing, then hunt a hidden break with an AI scan. Half of SpliceAI2's rare-disease splice hits sit >50 bp into introns (toy splice-graph model, real paper numbers).

title: Red-team 16 agents. Deploy 500.
mechanism: A 4-level game: red-team 16 AI agents (they die out), deploy 500 (they take off), pin the tipping point on the curve, then add teamwork. With the paper's Fig. 7 numbers the critical population is ≈463, a strong Allee effect.

title: Data buys the hand. Not the object.
mechanism: A 3-level game: feed a robot world model up to 3M hours of first-person video, pin the hand with a skeleton (50x less data), then grow the model. The hand sharpens to its 0.80 ceiling; the grasped object stalls at 0.565, and a 4x model adds only +0.034.

title: Keep the rollout alive
mechanism: One set of weights must denoise this frame and write memory for the next ones. With gradients 104° apart, no shared compromise survives a long rollout; split weights do.

title: The paper says 4. Lean proved 5.
mechanism: Slide the derivative budget behind Lemma 8.6: Lean certifies the theorem written in Lean, not the lemma printed in the paper.

title: Optimizer race: SGD vs Momentum vs RMSProp vs Adam
mechanism: Same loss surface, same start: watch how each update rule turns the same gradient into a different path.
